correctness.rationale: The exact full-domain proof derives the centered evaluation Green kernel from resistance, integrates it along each physical unit edge, substitutes the verified complete-multipartite Laplacian pseudoinverse, and compares all edge profiles pointwise. The key inequality alpha_12-(B_1-B_2)>0 holds exactly when minimum degree is at least three, with separate complete analyses of bipartite and all-singleton cases; the degree-one/two endpoint and circle exceptions are covered. All equality functions are obtained from the Riesz representer. The supplied self-contained rational checker independently verifies 2,910 vertex/orbit identities, 63 size profiles, 33 subdivided-edge integrations, 22 independent double integrals and seven exact constants. Finite tests are not asserted to prove the universal claim.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected primary results provide metric-graph resistance Green theory and discrete vertex resistances, but not an arclength-mean-zero sharp evaluation norm for arbitrary complete multipartite size profiles, not the strict two-largest-part edge comparison, and not the minimum-degree-three complete localization theorem. The previously available complete-bipartite case is acknowledged and included only as a covered special case, while the claim extends to all part numbers and low-degree exceptions. Searches did not locate explicit equivalent or dominating formulas. An inaccessible related primary source and possible implicit corollary coverage remain genuine bibliographic risks.

value.rationale: The problem is the exact optimal energy-to-supremum embedding on a standard class of metric graphs, with a natural and independently motivated localization question. The classification applies to every number of complete multipartite classes and all positive class sizes and uncovers a universal minimum-degree-three transition, with exceptions consisting of two circles. Explicit constants, strict size-based screening, location deficits, and all Green extremizers go beyond a routine single-parameter or finite-table evaluation. The previously solved bipartite subfamily is acknowledged as a restricted case.
